Description: The two bodies lie across each other rather than along each other, meeting at the hips at roughly a right angle with the legs crossed between. Seen from above the pair form an X, which is the whole reason for the name.

Variations: The crossing angle can open toward parallel or close toward perpendicular, and either partner can be the one lying flat.

On camera: The only position in this family that genuinely needs an overhead shot. In profile the crossing disappears entirely and it looks like a side-lying position.

AI design considerations: Two figures whose long axes cross near the pelvis at a wide angle. The crossing angle must be clearly non-zero, since near-parallel figures collapse the shape.

poses.name: The Drill
poses.description:
Description: A face-to-face position in which the receiving partner locks the ankles behind the penetrating partner's back and pulls, so the two pelvises stay clamped and the stroke shortens to almost nothing. The lock is the mechanism, and it converts a long stroke into sustained pressure.

Variations: Ankles crossed at the small of the back or higher between the shoulder blades; arms around the neck to add pull from above.

On camera: The clamp hides the contact point, so it reads as intensity rather than as explicit action, and productions use it for exactly that.

AI design considerations: Two stacked figures with the lower one's ankles crossed behind the upper one's back. The crossed ankles must sit behind the far body, which is the detail renders most often put in front.

poses.name: Spread Eagle
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner lies flat with both arms and both legs stretched wide, and the penetrating partner works above. Nothing is folded or held, which makes it the most open of the supine positions and the easiest to shoot from directly overhead.

Variations: Wrists held down by the partner's hands, legs wide and flat or lifted slightly, and the whole shape reversed into a prone spread.

On camera: The only common penetrative position that is fully legible from above, so it is the standard choice when a production wants an overhead master shot.

AI design considerations: A supine figure with all four limbs abducted and no flexion anywhere. Symmetry is the point here, unlike most positions in this catalog, where symmetry is a rendering error.

poses.name: The Gap
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner's hips are propped high on a cushion while the shoulders stay flat, opening a visible gap between the lower back and the surface, and the penetrating partner kneels into the raised angle. The gap is both the name and the entire mechanism.

Variations: Height of the prop sets the angle, and the legs can be flat, raised, or resting on the partner's shoulders without changing the underlying position.

On camera: The lift keeps the contact point clear of the surface, which is why it appears constantly in production under a dozen different names.

AI design considerations: A supine figure with a wedge under the sacrum and daylight under the lumbar spine. Rendering the gap is the whole job, since a body flat on the surface is a different position.

poses.name: The Hinge
poses.description:
Description: Both partners kneel one behind the other, and the front partner leans back onto locked arms so the torso opens away from the body behind. The lean is the hinge, and it turns an upright kneeling position into something with a working angle.

Variations: Hands on the floor behind or on the partner's thighs, and the depth of the lean sets the depth of entry. Sitting fully upright closes the hinge and ends the position.

On camera: The open torso is exactly what an upright kneeling position hides, so this is the version productions reach for when they need a rear-entry shape with the front of the body visible.

AI design considerations: Two kneeling figures stacked front to back, the forward one leaning back at roughly thirty degrees with weight through the arms. The lean angle is the identifying feature.

poses.name: The Ladder
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner bends forward onto a flight of steps, hands two or three risers up, while the penetrating partner stands on a lower step. The staircase does the work a height difference otherwise would, which is the only reason the position exists as a named thing.

Variations: How far up the hands are placed sets the angle of the back; the standing partner can move a step up or down mid-scene to change depth.

On camera: The diagonal of the staircase gives the frame a line that a flat set cannot, and it is shot in profile almost without exception.

AI design considerations: A hinged-forward figure with hands on an ascending surface and the partner behind on a lower plane. Without the stepped geometry it is an ordinary standing bend.

poses.name: Lifted Missionary
poses.description:
Description: The penetrating partner kneels and takes the receiving partner's hips off the surface entirely, holding the weight in both hands. It differs from every propped variant in that nothing supports the lift except the partner, so the angle can change continuously through a take.

Variations: Hands under the small of the back or under the buttocks, the receiving partner's shoulders staying down while the whole pelvis travels.

On camera: The floating pelvis and the visible effort are both part of the appeal, and it is one of the few positions where a point-of-view shot shows the mechanism rather than hiding it.

AI design considerations: A supine figure whose pelvis is unsupported and clearly held by two hands. The hands must be carrying load, and the lumbar spine has to extend to make the lift plausible.

poses.name: Magic Mountain
poses.description:
Description: A bank of cushions is built into a slope and the receiving partner kneels forward over it with the chest supported, while the penetrating partner kneels behind and leans back onto their own heels. Both partners are supported, which is the point: it is a position built to be held for a long time.

Variations: Height of the bank sets the angle, and the rear partner can sit fully back on the heels or rise up to change depth.

On camera: The cushion bank is awkward set dressing and reads as domestic rather than staged, so this appears far more in illustration than in production.

AI design considerations: Two figures both supported at an angle by a wedge of soft mass between them. The prop is structural here rather than decorative, and omitting it leaves the pair floating.

poses.name: The Peg
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner lies on one side with the lower leg straight and the upper leg raised nearly vertical, and the penetrating partner kneels straddling the lower thigh. The vertical leg is the peg, and holding it upright is what keeps the hips open.

Variations: Upper leg held at the calf, at the ankle, or resting along the partner's chest. Lowering it collapses the position into an ordinary side entry.

On camera: The near-vertical leg gives a strong graphic line and leaves the whole front of the body open, which is why the shape recurs under several different names.

AI design considerations: A side-lying figure with one leg flat and one close to vertical, and a kneeling figure between them. The ninety-degree separation between the two legs is the identifying detail.

poses.name: Rocking Horse
poses.description:
Description: The penetrating partner sits in a chair and the receiving partner straddles the lap facing them, feet on the floor, driving a forward and back rocking against the chair back. The chair is load bearing: it takes the rear partner's weight so all of the receiving partner's effort goes into the motion.

Variations: Feet on the floor or hooked over the chair arms, hands on the shoulders or on the chair back behind. Leaning back changes it from a rock to a bounce.

On camera: Furniture gives the frame structure and the standing height puts the action at natural camera level, which is why chair positions are a production staple.

AI design considerations: A seated figure in a chair with a straddling figure above, feet reaching the floor. The chair has to be drawn, and the receiving partner's feet must actually reach, or the weight has nowhere to go.

poses.name: The Scoop
poses.description:
Description: Both partners lie on the same side with the receiving partner curled forward into a tight C and the penetrating partner nested into the curve behind. The forward curl is what separates it from ordinary spooning: it opens the angle from behind without either partner rolling.

Variations: Depth of the curl, upper knee drawn toward the chest or left straight, and the rear partner's top arm over the waist or under the head.

On camera: The curl leaves a visible gap at the hips that flat spooning does not, so it is the version chosen when the shot has to show anything at all.

AI design considerations: Two side-lying figures with strongly matched C curves, the rear one nested inside the front one's arc. Parallel straight spines produce spooning instead.

poses.name: The Sidewinder
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner's shoulders stay flat on the surface while the hips rotate onto one side, and the penetrating partner kneels into the twist. The torso is deliberately wrung: shoulders square to the ceiling, pelvis square to the wall.

Variations: Degree of the twist, and which side the hips fall to. Letting the shoulders follow the hips converts it into a plain side-lying position.

On camera: The wrung torso keeps the chest facing the lens while the hips present from the side, so it delivers two framings at once. That combination is why it survives in production.

AI design considerations: Deliberate counter-rotation between shoulder girdle and pelvis in the lower figure. Most renders align the two and lose the entire position.

poses.name: Snow Angel
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner lies on the back and the penetrating partner lies face down on top but reversed, head toward the receiving partner's feet. It is a stack with the top figure turned end for end, and the required rotation is what makes it a stunt rather than a staple.

Variations: Full reversal, or a partial turn with the upper body angled off to one side to relieve the joint.

On camera: The reversal is only obvious from overhead or wide profile. It is shot as a set piece and rarely sustained.

AI design considerations: Two stacked figures with opposed head directions. The hip joints have to be drawn at the limit of external rotation, and getting them wrong is the usual tell.

poses.name: Sofa Brace
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner kneels on a sofa seat and folds forward over the back or the arm, chest supported, while the penetrating partner stands or kneels behind. The furniture takes the upper body weight, which is why this shape appears in almost every domestic set.

Variations: Over the back of the sofa or over the arm, knees on the seat or feet on the floor, and the chest fully down or propped on the forearms.

On camera: Furniture puts the action at a workable height and gives the frame a horizontal edge to compose against. One of the most shot positions on any domestic set.

AI design considerations: A kneeling figure folded forward over a raised horizontal edge with the chest supported. The furniture is load bearing and has to be drawn at the right height, or the fold has nothing to rest on.

poses.name: Squat Thrust
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner squats over the supine penetrating partner on the feet rather than the knees, facing them, and drives a full vertical rise and fall. Working from the feet gives far more travel than a kneeling straddle and costs far more effort.

Variations: Hands braced on the chest, on the surface behind, or free. Dropping to the knees at any point converts it into an ordinary astride position.

On camera: The full stroke length is visible in a way no kneeling position can match, which is exactly why it is shot despite being unsustainable for long.

AI design considerations: A deep squat above a supine figure with both feet flat and the knees outside the elbows. Heels lifting off is the usual error and it makes the balance impossible.

poses.name: The Stairway
poses.description:
Description: The penetrating partner sits on a step with the feet two risers down, and the receiving partner sits into the lap facing them with their own feet lower still. The staircase provides the height offset that a flat floor cannot, and both partners keep contact with a solid surface throughout.

Variations: Which step each partner takes sets the angle. Facing away instead converts it into a rear-entry seated position on the same geometry.

On camera: The stair diagonal and the raised height make it a favorite for hallway and entryway sets. Wide profile is the only framing that shows the geometry.

AI design considerations: Two seated figures at different heights with a stepped surface behind. The step offset is the whole position and a flat floor removes its reason to exist.

poses.name: Stand and Deliver
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner stands and bends forward with the hands braced on their own knees or thighs rather than on any furniture, while the penetrating partner stands behind. Self-bracing is what distinguishes it: nothing in the room is carrying any load.

Variations: Hands on the knees, on the shins, or reaching to the floor, with the depth of the bend setting the angle. Feet apart for stability or together to tighten the fit.

On camera: Set independent, so it can be shot anywhere. The absence of furniture makes it read as spontaneous, which is why it recurs in location scenes.

AI design considerations: A standing figure hinged at the hips with hands on its own legs and no external support. The knees should be softly bent, since locked knees at that hinge angle are not sustainable.

poses.name: Tabletop
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner sits or lies back on a table or counter at hip height with the legs raised, and the penetrating partner stands at the edge. The height match is the entire idea, and it removes every strength requirement that standing positions normally carry.

Variations: Fully reclined or propped on the elbows, legs held wide, over the shoulders, or wrapped around the waist. Any waist-height surface works.

On camera: Extremely common because the surface sets a repeatable height, keeps both performers stable and puts the action at lens level without a rig.

AI design considerations: A supine or reclined figure on a raised horizontal plane with a standing figure at the edge. Get the surface height right at the standing figure's hip, since a wrong height makes the geometry impossible.

poses.name: Teaspoon
poses.description:
Description: A side-lying rear entry in which the receiving partner's upper leg is lifted and held high rather than resting along the lower one. Opening that leg is what turns a closed spooning position into a working one with a real angle.

Variations: The leg held by the partner at the knee or the ankle, or supported on the partner's shoulder. Lowering it closes back into ordinary spooning.

On camera: The raised leg is what makes the difference on screen: it opens the contact point that flat spooning conceals completely, at no cost in effort.

AI design considerations: Two side-lying figures with the front one's upper leg abducted and elevated. The lift angle is the identifying feature and should be well past horizontal.

poses.name: The Pump
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner lies back with the hips right at the edge of the bed and the legs up, while the penetrating partner stands on the floor. The floor gives the standing partner full leg drive, which no kneeling position on a soft surface can match.

Variations: Legs held wide, folded to the chest, or resting on the standing partner's shoulders. Ankles gripped for leverage is the most common working form.

On camera: The single most repeatable setup in production: fixed height, fixed marks, full visibility and the performer's feet on solid ground.

AI design considerations: A supine figure with the pelvis at a surface edge and a standing figure on a lower plane. The floor and the mattress must be at different heights, or the drive angle makes no sense.

poses.name: The Tree
poses.description:
Description: Both partners kneel upright and face to face, torsos vertical and thighs interlocked, with one partner's knees inside the other's. The whole shape is columnar, which is where the name comes from, and it works entirely from small hip movement.

Variations: Arms around the shoulders or the waist, one partner sitting back onto the heels to lower the height, and the knees interlocked or side by side.

On camera: The vertical stack of two upright bodies reads as intimacy and shoots well in a close two-shot, but the contact point is hidden between the thighs.

AI design considerations: Two kneeling figures at the same height with vertical torsos and interlocked thighs. Keep the heads level, since the vertical symmetry is the whole visual idea.

poses.name: The Twister
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner lies on one side with the upper body rotated back toward the ceiling and one leg carried across the body, while the penetrating partner kneels into the resulting opening. The rotation runs the opposite way to the sidewinder, so the twist sits in the lower spine rather than the upper.

Variations: The crossed leg held high or dropped low, and the shoulder rotation held or released to change the depth of the wring.

On camera: The corkscrew line is unusual enough to be worth a shot in itself, but it is hard to hold and generally cut short.

AI design considerations: A side-lying figure with the pelvis rotated one way and the shoulders the other, plus a leg crossing the midline. Three rotations in one body is the hardest geometry in this batch to keep anatomically legal.

poses.name: The X
poses.description:
Description: Both partners lie on their backs facing away from each other with the legs scissored at the hips, so from above the pair form a clean X with the heads at opposite corners. Neither partner supports the other and the movement comes entirely from the hips.

Variations: The crossing angle can be opened or closed, and either partner can prop up on the elbows to see the other.

On camera: A purely overhead position. From the side it is unreadable, and that limitation is why it appears far more in diagrams than in video.

AI design considerations: Two supine figures with heads at opposite ends and legs interleaved at the pelvis. The X should be obvious from above, which means the torsos need a wide angle between them, not a narrow one.

poses.name: Reverse Piledriver
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner is inverted on the shoulders as in a standard piledriver, but turned to face away, so the penetrating partner squats above entering from behind rather than in front. The reversal changes the angle of the spine and puts the receiving partner's face out of the frame entirely.

Variations: Legs spread wide or held together above, hips braced against a wall or headboard, and the squat taken high or dropped low.

On camera: Shot low and in profile. It is the most physically demanding position in the catalog to hold and is filmed in very short takes.

AI design considerations: An inverted figure supported on the shoulders with the pelvis above the head and the body turned away from the partner. The reversal is the only thing separating it from the standard piledriver, so the facing must be unambiguous.

poses.name: Froggy Style
poses.description:
Description: A rear-entry position in which the receiving partner squats forward on the feet rather than kneeling, hands down, knees wide outside the elbows. Being on the feet instead of the knees raises the hips and opens the stance far more than an all-fours position does.

Variations: Hands flat on the surface or on a raised object, heels down or lifted, and the knees carried wide or drawn in.

On camera: The wide crouch is legible in profile and from behind, and the higher hip line keeps the contact point clear of the surface.

AI design considerations: A deep forward squat with hands down, feet flat and knees abducted well outside the arms. The feet, not the knees, must carry the weight, which is what separates it from an all-fours pose.

poses.name: Kneeling Wheelbarrow
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner takes their weight on the hands while the penetrating partner kneels and holds the thighs, rather than standing. Kneeling drops the whole arrangement close to the surface, which cuts the strain on the receiving partner's shoulders enough to make it holdable.

Variations: Legs held at the thighs or hooked over the partner's shoulders, and the receiving partner on straight arms or dropped to the forearms.

On camera: The lower height keeps both bodies in one frame without a wide lens, which the standing form does not allow.

AI design considerations: An inverted-torso figure supported on the arms with the hips held at the partner's kneeling height. The shoulder load has to look real, and the arms should show compression rather than resting straight.

poses.name: Fire Hydrant
poses.description:
Description: A rear-entry position on all fours with one of the receiving partner's knees lifted out to the side. The asymmetry opens one hip completely while the other stays planted, which is both the mechanical point and the source of the name.

Variations: The raised leg held by the partner or held under its own power, lifted to the side or carried forward. Swapping legs mid-scene reverses the angle.

On camera: The lifted leg opens the contact point in a way that a symmetric all-fours position cannot, which is why it appears so often as a variation beat within a longer rear-entry take.

AI design considerations: An all-fours figure with one hip abducted to roughly ninety degrees and three limbs still planted. The lifted side pulls the pelvis with it, so the hips should not stay level.

poses.name: Bucking Bronco
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner straddles facing away and leans far forward, gripping the penetrating partner's shins or ankles for leverage, and drives from the legs. The extreme forward lean is what distinguishes it: it steepens the angle well past anything an upright reverse straddle produces.

Variations: Hands on the shins, on the ankles, or planted on the surface beyond the feet. Feet flat for a squatting drive or knees down for a slower one.

On camera: The signature rear-facing shot in production, because the forward lean presents the whole back line and keeps the contact point in frame throughout.

AI design considerations: A reversed straddling figure hinged well forward at the hips with the arms reaching down the partner's legs. The lean angle is the identifying feature and an upright torso turns it into an ordinary reverse straddle.

poses.name: Praying Mantis
poses.description:
Description: Both partners kneel one behind the other with the torsos fully upright and the receiving partner's arms raised or folded high across the chest. The tall, narrow silhouette with the raised forearms is what the name is describing.

Variations: Arms raised overhead, folded across the chest, or reaching back to the partner's neck. Leaning either partner forward converts it into a different position entirely.

On camera: A vertical composition with no occlusion of the upper body, which makes it useful for showing the receiving partner's face and torso while an entry from behind is still in progress.

AI design considerations: Two kneeling figures stacked front to back with both spines vertical and the forward figure's arms elevated. The raised arms are the identifying detail and are the first thing a default pose drops.

poses.name: Reverse Spoon
poses.description:
Description: Spooning turned around: both partners lie on their sides but face to face, with the receiving partner's upper leg draped over the partner's hip. It keeps the low effort of spooning while restoring eye contact, which is the whole reason to switch.

Variations: Upper leg draped, hooked behind, or lifted and held. Arms usually under the head and around the waist rather than doing any work.

On camera: Both faces are available in a single profile frame, which is exactly what standard spooning cannot deliver, so it is the version used whenever reactions matter.

AI design considerations: Two side-lying figures facing each other with pelvises in contact and one leg draped. The difference from the twining position is that only one leg crosses here rather than an alternating weave.

poses.name: Seated Scissoring
poses.description:
Description: Both partners sit facing each other and lean back onto their hands with the legs scissored, so contact is made and held at the hips. Sitting up rather than lying down puts both faces in the same frame and lets either partner control the pressure.

Variations: Both partners propped on straight arms, on the elbows, or one upright and one reclined. Legs scissored at the knee or interlocked further up.

On camera: The open V of the two bodies leaves the contact point unobstructed from the side, which is why this is the standard framing for the act rather than the supine version.

AI design considerations: Two seated figures leaning back on the arms with legs interleaved at the pelvis. Both torsos angle back at roughly the same degree, and the leg weave carries the contact.

poses.name: Reverse Amazon
poses.description:
Description: The penetrating partner lies with the knees drawn up toward the chest while the receiving partner squats over facing away, using the folded legs as a backrest. The fold shortens the working length considerably, and turning away changes which surfaces take the contact.

Variations: Depth of the partner's leg fold, and whether the receiving partner squats on the feet or settles onto the knees.

On camera: Shot from behind or low in profile. The folded lower figure is unusual enough in silhouette that the position is recognizable even in a still.

AI design considerations: A supine figure with knees folded toward the chest and a reversed squatting figure above. The fold on the lower figure is the identifying feature and separates it from a plain reverse straddle.

poses.name: Over the Edge
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner lies face down with the torso on the bed and the hips out past the edge, feet toward the floor, while the penetrating partner stands behind. It is the prone counterpart of the standing edge positions and it gives the standing partner the same solid footing.

Variations: Feet on the floor or hooked back around the partner's legs, torso flat or propped on the forearms, and the hips at the edge or further out.

On camera: The change in plane at the mattress edge gives the frame a clean line and puts the action at standing height without a lift.

AI design considerations: A prone figure whose pelvis extends past a surface edge with the legs descending toward a lower plane. The edge has to be visible, since it is the only thing that explains the geometry.

poses.name: The Chairman
poses.description:
Description: The penetrating partner sits upright in a chair and the receiving partner lowers into the lap facing away, feet on the floor either side. The chair back supports one partner completely, so all the movement comes from the receiving partner's legs.

Variations: Feet on the floor, on the chair rail, or knees on the seat. Leaning back against the partner's chest or forward onto the knees changes the depth.

On camera: The chair sets a fixed height and the outward-facing body leaves the front fully open, which makes this one of the most reliable setups on any furnished set.

AI design considerations: A seated figure in a chair with a second figure lowered into the lap facing away, feet reaching the floor. Draw the chair: without it the lower figure has no support and the height is unexplained.

poses.name: Cross Position
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner lies on the back with the legs raised, and the penetrating partner lies on one side at a right angle across them, so the two bodies meet at the hips in a cross. Neither partner supports any of the other's weight, which is what makes it holdable for a long stretch.

Variations: The receiving partner's legs over the partner's hips or resting on the partner's shoulder, and the crossing angle opened toward parallel to change the depth.

On camera: Legible from overhead and, unusually for a crossed position, also readable in profile because the raised legs mark the junction.

AI design considerations: Two figures whose long axes meet at roughly ninety degrees at the pelvis, one supine and one on its side. The right angle is the identifying feature and is what separates it from the criss-cross, where both partners lie back.

poses.name: Drunken Boat
poses.description:
Description: Both partners sit facing each other with the legs interlocked and lean back onto their hands, then rock the shared centre of mass back and forth as though working a small boat. The motion is cooperative and neither partner leads it, which is unusual enough to have earned the position a name of its own.

Variations: Hands joined and pulling against each other instead of planted behind, which converts the rock into a see-saw with a longer travel.

On camera: The symmetric open V is a clean composition from the side, and the slow shared rhythm suits longer takes than most seated positions.

AI design considerations: Two mirrored seated figures leaning back with legs interlocked at the hips. Symmetry is deliberate here, and the two lean angles should match rather than one dominating.

poses.name: The Corkscrew
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner lies on one side at the edge of the bed with both legs together and extended over the edge, while the penetrating partner stands. Keeping the legs closed and rotated to one side narrows the angle sharply, which is the entire reason to choose it.

Variations: Legs straight out or bent at the knee, and the receiving partner rolled further toward the mattress or back toward the ceiling to change the twist.

On camera: The standing partner and the horizontal body line make a strong right-angle composition, and the closed legs read as tension in a way open positions do not.

AI design considerations: A side-lying figure at a surface edge with legs together and a standing figure alongside. The closed legs are the identifying feature, so avoid the default abduction a side-lying skeleton usually carries.

poses.name: The Plow
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner takes a shoulder stand and folds the legs back past the head, and the penetrating partner stands or kneels above entering downward. It is the deepest fold in the catalog and demands hamstring and spinal range that very few people have without preparation.

Variations: Legs folded to either side of the head rather than together, and the fold supported by the partner's hands rather than held.

On camera: A set piece rather than a working position. It is filmed in short takes and almost always low and in profile so the fold reads.

AI design considerations: An inverted figure with the hips above the shoulders and both legs carried past the head line. Neck load is the anatomical trap: weight belongs on the shoulders and upper back, never the cervical spine.

poses.name: The Wraparound
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner sits upright on the edge of a table or counter and wraps both legs around the standing partner's waist, pulling them in. It reads as a carry but the surface takes all the weight, so it costs almost nothing to hold.

Variations: Ankles crossed behind the back or hooked at the knees, arms around the neck, and the receiving partner leaning back on the hands to open the angle.

On camera: Looks like a standing lift while being sustainable for a full take, which is exactly why productions favor it over a real carry.

AI design considerations: A seated figure on a raised edge with both legs wrapped around a standing figure. The buttocks must stay in contact with the surface, or the pose becomes a carry and the load path changes completely.

poses.name: Deep Throat
poses.description:
Description: Oral contact taken to full depth, with the giving partner kneeling and the head angled so that mouth and throat line up on a single axis. The alignment is the technique: without it the depth is not available at any angle.

Variations: Kneeling with the head tipped back, or lying with the head over an edge, which achieves the same alignment with less neck work. Hands on the head or free.

On camera: Shot close and in profile so the throat line is visible, and it is the single most filmed oral variation in the medium.

AI design considerations: A kneeling figure with the cervical spine extended so the head, neck and torso form a continuous line. The extended neck is the identifying feature and a neutral head position depicts a different act.

poses.name: The Pinball Wizard
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner takes a shoulder stand with the back braced against a wall or the front of a couch, which holds the inversion without any core work, and the penetrating partner kneels above. The brace is what separates it from a piledriver, where the receiving partner carries the whole hold.

Variations: Braced against a wall, a couch front or a headboard. Legs spread, held together, or hooked over the partner's shoulders.

On camera: The wall gives the frame a vertical reference that a free inversion lacks, and the support means the position holds long enough to actually shoot.

AI design considerations: An inverted figure with the back flat against a vertical plane and the hips above the shoulders. The wall contact has to carry visible load, otherwise this renders as an unsupported piledriver.

poses.name: Cunnilingus from Behind
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner kneels on all fours and the giving partner works from behind, lying or crouching low. Approaching from the rear rather than the front changes which surfaces are reachable and is the only thing distinguishing it from the supine variants.

Variations: The receiving partner on all fours or with the chest dropped to the surface, and the giving partner lying prone or crouched on the knees and elbows.

On camera: Shot from the side or behind. The low giving position sits mostly out of frame, so productions usually favor a close framing over a wide one.

AI design considerations: An all-fours figure with a prone or low-crouched figure behind at hip height. The height relationship is the hard part: the giving figure's head has to reach without the neck bending past its range.

poses.name: Cunnilingus, receiving seated
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner sits on a chair or the edge of a seat with the hips forward and the legs open, while the giving partner kneels on the floor in front. The chair sets the height, which is why this is the most comfortable of the oral positions to hold for any length of time.

Variations: Legs over the partner's shoulders, feet on the chair rail, or one foot up on the seat. The receiving partner reclined against the chair back or sitting forward.

On camera: Furniture puts both performers at fixed marks and the seated partner's face stays fully available, which the lying variants make difficult.

AI design considerations: A seated figure with hips forward on a chair and a kneeling figure between the knees. The chair has to be drawn and the seated pelvis should sit near the front edge, not back in the seat.

poses.name: Anilingus (receiving prone)
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner lies fully prone with the hips flat or slightly propped, and the giving partner lies behind and below. Lying rather than kneeling means neither partner is holding a position, so it is the least demanding form of the act.

Variations: Hips flat or raised on a cushion, legs together or parted, and the giving partner prone or propped on the elbows.

On camera: Almost entirely a close framing. In a wide shot the two flat bodies read as a single mass and the act is not visible at all.

AI design considerations: Two prone figures offset lengthwise with the lower one's head at the upper one's hips. Keep a clear vertical separation, or the overlapping silhouettes merge.

poses.name: Thigh Riding
poses.description:
Description: One partner sits and the other straddles a single thigh rather than the lap, grinding against it. Nothing is penetrative and usually nothing is removed, which makes it one of the few positions in the catalog that works fully clothed.

Variations: Straddling face to face or facing away, the seated partner flexing the thigh to add pressure, and the straddling partner supported at the hips or moving unaided.

On camera: Reads as build-up rather than act, so it appears in opening sequences and in clothed scenes where nothing more explicit is available.

AI design considerations: A seated figure with one thigh raised and a second figure straddling that single leg rather than the hips. The offset to one side is the identifying detail: centered over the lap makes it a different position.

poses.name: Face-to-Face Tribbing
poses.description:
Description: One partner lies supine and the other lies fully on top, chest to chest, with contact and pressure carried at the hips. Unlike the scissored forms the bodies stay aligned rather than crossed, so it trades visibility for full-length contact and eye contact.

Variations: Legs interleaved or the upper partner's knees outside the lower partner's hips, and one leg drawn up to change the angle of pressure.

On camera: The stacked bodies occlude the contact point almost completely, so it is shot for the faces and the movement rather than the act, which is exactly the opposite of the scissored version.

AI design considerations: Two aligned figures in full-length contact with pelvises engaged. The distinguishing detail against scissoring is that both long axes point the same way rather than crossing.

poses.name: Double Cowgirl
poses.description:
Description: One partner lies supine while a second straddles the hips and a third kneels over the face, both facing the same direction. It is the most common three-person arrangement built on a single supine base, and it works because the two upper partners occupy positions that do not compete for space.

Variations: The two upper partners facing each other or both facing the same way, and either one turning to face away. Swapping which of the two takes the hips is the usual mid-scene change.

On camera: Shot in profile and slightly low so all three bodies stay separable. The vertical stack is what makes it legible where most three-person arrangements are not.

AI design considerations: A supine base with two figures above at different points along its length. Keep them clearly separated along the axis, since overlapping upper figures collapse into an unreadable mass.

poses.name: The Sandwich
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner lies face down on a supine partner while a third enters from above and behind, so all three bodies stack horizontally. The lying base is what distinguishes it from the standing sandwich: nobody is carrying weight, so it holds far longer.

Variations: The base partner's legs extended or bent for bracing, and the top partner kneeling astride or in a full plank. The middle partner can face down or turn to the side to relieve the chest.

On camera: Profile only. From any other angle the three bodies merge, and the layered silhouette is the entire visual proposition.

AI design considerations: Three horizontally stacked figures with distinct vertical offsets. Each layer needs its own visible outline, which means staggering the shoulder positions rather than aligning them.

poses.name: Cross Double Penetration
poses.description:
Description: A double arrangement in which the two penetrating partners work at crossed angles rather than in line, one supine beneath and one kneeling well off to the side. Breaking the alignment gives both partners room to move independently, which the stacked version does not.

Variations: The crossing angle can be opened toward ninety degrees or closed toward the standard in-line form; the receiving partner leans away from the kneeling partner to open the approach.

On camera: The offset keeps three bodies separable in a single profile frame, which is exactly the problem the in-line version has.

AI design considerations: A supine base with a straddling figure rotated off axis and a third kneeling at a clear angle to both. The non-alignment is the identifying feature and a symmetric arrangement depicts a different position.

poses.name: Bunk Beds
poses.description:
Description: Two pairs stacked one above the other, the upper pair supported on the lower pair's raised knees and hands. It is a staged arrangement rather than a working one: the load path is real but marginal, and it exists to be photographed.

Variations: The upper pair carried on the lower pair's shins, or supported partly by furniture at the head and feet to make the stack survivable.

On camera: Wide profile is the only framing that shows both tiers. The whole point is the two-level silhouette, which no other arrangement in the catalog produces.

AI design considerations: Four figures in two clearly separated horizontal bands with a visible support structure between them. The upper tier needs a plausible load path down into the lower one, or the stack reads as figures floating.

poses.name: The Shoulder Ride
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner sits on the standing partner's shoulders, thighs either side of the head, while the standing partner holds the legs and takes oral contact from below. It is a carry and an oral position at once, and the balance requirement is what keeps it rare.

Variations: Performed free standing, or with the receiving partner's back braced against a wall so the standing partner only carries weight rather than balance as well.

On camera: Framed wide and low, since the whole proposition is the height of the arrangement. Takes are short because the load is carried entirely on the neck and shoulders.

AI design considerations: A standing figure with a second figure seated across its shoulders, hands gripping the thighs. The load has to travel down through the standing spine, so expect a visible counter-lean rather than an upright stance.

poses.name: Standing Carry, Rear Entry
poses.description:
Description: A full standing carry with the receiving partner facing away rather than toward the partner, held under the thighs with the back against the partner's chest. Turning the carry around removes the arms-around-the-neck grip that makes a face-to-face lift stable, so the carrying partner takes the entire load unaided.

Variations: Arms hooked back around the partner's neck, or reaching down to the partner's forearms. The receiving partner's back against a wall converts it into a supported lift and roughly halves the effort.

On camera: The outward-facing body presents the whole front to the lens, which is exactly what a face-to-face carry hides. Shot wide and slightly low, in short takes.

AI design considerations: One figure carried at hip height facing away, supported under both thighs. Without a neck grip the carrying figure needs a deep counter-lean, and drawing it upright makes the balance impossible.

poses.name: Piledriver Double Penetration
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner is inverted on the shoulders as in a piledriver while one partner squats above and a second works from the side, taking the two entry points at once. The inversion opens an angle that no horizontal double arrangement produces, and it is the most demanding three-person hold in the catalog.

Variations: The second partner kneeling rather than squatting, the hips braced against a headboard or wall, and the legs held apart by whichever partner is above.

On camera: Shot low and in profile so the inversion registers against the two working partners. Very short takes, since nobody can hold it long.

AI design considerations: An inverted figure with the pelvis above the head line and two figures converging above it. Three bodies in a tight vertical stack fuse easily, so each needs its own clear silhouette edge.

poses.name: Seated Double Penetration
poses.description:
Description: One partner sits and the receiving partner lowers into the lap facing away, while a second partner kneels in front and enters from the other side. The seated base carries the weight, which is what lets a double arrangement hold longer here than in any standing or inverted version.

Variations: On a chair, a sofa or the floor. The front partner kneeling or standing depending on the seat height, and the receiving partner leaning back against the chest or forward onto the front partner.

On camera: Furniture fixes the height and keeps all three at workable marks, which is why this shape recurs on domestic sets where the horizontal versions do not fit the frame.

AI design considerations: A seated base with a second figure in the lap and a third kneeling ahead of them. The seat must be drawn and load-bearing, or the middle figure has nothing holding it at that height.

poses.name: Prone Double Penetration
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner lies face down over a supine partner while a third works from above and behind, so both entries come from the rear rather than one from each side. It is the flattest of the double arrangements and the only one where all three spines run roughly parallel.

Variations: Hips propped on a cushion to open the upper angle, the base partner's legs spread for bracing, and the top partner kneeling astride rather than in a full plank.

On camera: Profile only. The three parallel bodies read as one mass from above and the arrangement disappears entirely from behind.

AI design considerations: Three horizontally stacked figures with parallel spines and staggered shoulders. Without the stagger the silhouettes merge into a single indistinct block.

poses.name: Wheelbarrow Double Penetration
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner takes their weight on the hands with the legs held by a standing partner behind, while a third works underneath from the front. The barrow hold puts the whole body horizontal and unsupported, so both working partners carry load as well as motion.

Variations: The front partner lying, kneeling or seated on a low surface depending on the barrow height, and the receiving partner on straight arms or dropped to the forearms.

On camera: A wide profile is the only framing that fits all three, and the horizontal middle figure gives the composition a strong line that no other double arrangement produces.

AI design considerations: A horizontal figure supported at the hands and thighs with two figures at either end. Arm compression has to be visible, since straight relaxed arms cannot carry that load.

poses.name: Suspended Double Penetration
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner is carried entirely off the ground between two standing partners, one supporting under the thighs from the front and one taking the weight from behind. Nothing touches a surface except four feet, which makes it the most physically extreme arrangement in the catalog.

Variations: Backed against a wall to transfer part of the load, or with one partner seated on a raised edge so only one is truly carrying.

On camera: Shot wide and low so the elevation reads. Takes are measured in seconds, and productions usually cut in from a supported version rather than starting here.

AI design considerations: One figure held at hip height between two upright figures, feet clear of the ground. Both carriers need deep counter-leans, and the arms under the thighs must show real load transfer.

poses.name: Folded Double Penetration
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner reclines back onto a supine partner with both knees drawn up and held wide, while a third kneels in front. Folding the legs back opens both entry points simultaneously without anyone having to change position mid-scene, which is why it is the most workable of the double arrangements.

Variations: Knees held by the front partner, by the base partner's hands under the thighs, or hooked over the front partner's shoulders.

On camera: The open fold keeps everything visible from a low profile angle, and all three faces stay in frame, which most double arrangements cannot manage.

AI design considerations: A supine base, a reclined figure on top with deep hip flexion, and a kneeling figure at the open end. The middle figure's back should follow the base's chest line rather than sitting upright.

poses.name: Standing Spit Roast
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner stands and bends forward at the hips, taking oral contact from a standing partner in front and rear entry from a standing partner behind. Everyone is on their feet, which distinguishes it from the ordinary spit roast where the middle partner kneels.

Variations: The front partner standing or seated on a raised edge to set the height, and the receiving partner's hands braced on the front partner's hips or on their own thighs.

On camera: All three bodies stay upright in one frame, which shoots far more cleanly than the kneeling version. Profile is the standard setup.

AI design considerations: Three upright figures with the middle one hinged forward at the hips. Height matching matters twice here, once at each contact point, so plan both before posing either.

poses.name: Kneeling Spit Roast
poses.description:
Description: All three partners kneel, the receiving partner upright between the other two rather than down on all fours. Keeping the middle partner vertical puts the whole front of the body in view and changes the working angle at both ends.

Variations: The front partner kneeling upright or sitting back on the heels to lower the oral height, and the rear partner sitting back to change the depth.

On camera: The three-body vertical column is unusual enough in silhouette to carry a wide shot, and unlike the standard spit roast the middle partner's face and torso stay available.

AI design considerations: Three kneeling figures in a line, the middle one upright rather than hinged. Keep the head heights staggered, since three level heads read as a chorus line rather than an arrangement.

poses.name: Seated Spit Roast
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner sits into one partner's lap facing away and leans forward to take oral contact from a second partner standing in front. The seated base does all the supporting, so the middle partner controls both contacts from one stable position.

Variations: The front partner standing or seated depending on the chair height, and the middle partner upright or folded well forward to change the oral angle.

On camera: Furniture sets repeatable marks for three performers, which is the practical reason seated group arrangements survive in production where standing ones do not.

AI design considerations: A seated base, a figure in the lap hinged forward, and a standing figure ahead. The forward hinge is the identifying detail: an upright middle figure makes the front contact impossible.

poses.name: Bridged Double Penetration
poses.description:
Description: The receiving partner holds an arched bridge over a supine partner, weight on the feet and shoulders, while a third kneels at the open end. The arch lifts the pelvis clear of the base partner's body and creates a working gap that a flat stack does not have.

Variations: The bridge held unaided or supported under the small of the back by either partner, and the arch shallow or extreme depending on what the middle partner can hold.

On camera: The raised arch gives the composition a clear negative space between the bodies, which is the one thing that makes a three-person profile shot legible.

AI design considerations: A strongly extended spine with hips at the apex and visible daylight beneath. If the arch collapses onto the base figure the position becomes an ordinary stacked double.

poses.name: Reverse Spit Roast
poses.description:
Description: The spit roast inverted: the middle partner kneels and gives oral to two partners standing or kneeling on either side, turning between them. The direction of service is what reverses, not the geometry, and the alternation is the whole mechanic.

Variations: The two outer partners standing, kneeling, or seated on an edge; the middle partner alternating or working both at once with hands.

On camera: Framed wide in profile so both outer partners stay in shot, and the turning motion gives the take a natural rhythm to cut on.

AI design considerations: A kneeling central figure flanked by two upright figures at matched height. The head turn toward one side is the identifying detail, and a forward-facing head makes the arrangement ambiguous.

poses.name: Double Facesitting
poses.description:
Description: One partner lies supine while two straddle in sequence along the body, the first over the face and the second over the hips, both facing the same way. It is the facesitting arrangement extended to three, and the two upper partners face each other across the lower one.

Variations: The two upper partners facing each other or back to back, and either one turning to reverse. Swapping which one takes the face is the usual mid-scene change.

On camera: Low and in profile so the two upper bodies separate cleanly, or overhead when the intent is the pair rather than the act.

AI design considerations: A supine base with two straddling figures at clearly different points along its length. Overlap between the upper figures is the usual failure, so keep them well separated along the axis.

poses.name: Stacked Oral
poses.description:
Description: Three partners lie in a stack where each gives oral to the one below and receives from the one above, a sixty-nine extended by one layer. Every partner is doing and receiving at once, which is what distinguishes it from arrangements where one person is the focus.

Variations: The stack laid flat or angled with the top partner propped, and the order rotated so a different partner takes the middle.

On camera: Overhead is the only framing that shows the chain. In profile the three bodies compress into a single horizontal band and the structure is lost.

AI design considerations: Three figures in alternating head-to-toe orientation with clear vertical separation between layers. The alternation is the whole structure and is the first thing a render flattens.

poses.name: Standing Line-Up
poses.description:
Description: Two receiving partners stand side by side and bend forward while a third works between them, moving from one to the other. The two are presented on the same plane at the same height, which is the entire staging idea and the reason it is shot rather than the sequential version.

Variations: Both bent over the same surface, braced on their own knees, or one standing and one kneeling to stagger the heights.

On camera: Shot from behind or in wide profile so both receiving partners stay in frame, and the alternation gives the editor a natural cut point.

AI design considerations: Two hinged-forward figures at matched height with one upright figure behind. The matched height is what makes the arrangement work, so avoid the size variation a render usually adds for interest.

poses.name: Double Manual
poses.description:
Description: Two partners kneel either side of a third who lies or reclines between them, both working by hand. Nothing is penetrative and neither partner needs to hold a position, which makes it one of the few group arrangements that can run for a long take without anyone tiring.

Variations: The central partner supine, seated, or reclined against one of the two; the outer partners alternating or working together.

On camera: A close framing, since the action is in the hands and a wide shot loses it entirely. Both outer faces stay available, which is most of why it gets used.
